albums.blurb: Eumir Deodato is the Brazilian keyboardist and arranger who worked with Antônio Carlos Jobim and Frank Sinatra before recording Prelude, his debut as a leader for Creed Taylor's CTI label. Its funk reworking of Strauss's "Also sprach Zarathustra" — the theme familiar from 2001: A Space Odyssey — made the album CTI's biggest seller, and the drum break opening "September 13" became one of the most sampled beats of early hip-hop. Six tracks of strings, Fender Rhodes, and a rhythm section including Stanley Clarke, Billy Cobham, and Airto Moreira — entirely instrumental.
albums.reception: The single edit of "Also sprach Zarathustra (2001)" reached No. 2 on the US pop chart and won the 1974 Grammy Award for Best Pop Instrumental Performance.

albums.blurb: The Montreal producer's studio debut, released on XL Recordings after years of SoundCloud remixes and beat tapes, folds house, funk, hip-hop, and R&B into fifteen tracks with guests including Anderson .Paak, Syd, Little Dragon, Craig David, and BADBADNOTGOOD. It remains the blueprint for the swung, off-grid groove that made his name and set up the follow-ups Bubba and Timeless.
albums.reception: It won the 2016 Polaris Music Prize and Electronic Album of the Year at the 2017 Juno Awards, and holds a Metacritic score of 81 out of 100.

albums.blurb: Haruomi Hosono — bassist of the pioneering Tokyo band Happy End and later co-founder of Yellow Magic Orchestra — made his solo debut with this set of laid-back country-folk and funk-tinged songs, recorded on a 16-track console in the bedroom of his house in Sayama outside Tokyo with the group that became Tin Pan Alley. Modeled partly on The Band's Music from Big Pink, it helped establish a homegrown strain of Japanese pop that later flowered into city pop.
albums.reception: Long a cult item outside Japan, it received its first official international release in 2018 through Light in the Attic's Hosono reissue series, and Harry Styles has credited it as the inspiration for the title of his 2022 album Harry's House.
